description: The plot illustrates the relationship between the Co-occurrence Number and ACC (%) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis is labeled "Co-occurrence Number" and employs a logarithmic scale for values above zero, with visible tick marks at 0, $10^1$, $10^2$, and $10^3$. The y-axis is labeled "ACC (%)" and uses a linear scale ranging from 60 to 85, with tick marks at regular intervals of 5 units. All six methods are represented by solid lines that demonstrate a steady upward trend across the four plotted data points along the x-axis. The "Base" method is represented by a black line with circle markers, increasing from approximately 63.8 at the first data point to 71.0 at the final data point. The "FT" method is shown as a blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers, rising from roughly 65.2 to 73.0. The "IKE" method is depicted by a red line with upward-pointing triangle markers, growing from about 67.4 to 75.2. The "MEMIT" method is shown as a purple line with pentagon markers, increasing from approximately 69.5 to 77.6. The "MEND" method is represented by a brown line with diamond markers, starting at roughly 70.7 and climbing to 80.1. Finally, the "ROME" method is depicted by a green line with square markers, showing an increase from approximately 74.3 at the initial data point to 84.1 at the final data point.
